title: Vanishing Cech H^1 of the kernel on a cofinal system of open coverings gives surjectivity on sections (O_X-modules)
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $0\to\mathcal F\xrightarrow{\iota}\mathcal G\xrightarrow{\varphi}\mathcal H\to0$ be a short exact sequence [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence] in the abelian category $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ of sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules on the underlying topological space of $X$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $U\subseteq X$ be an open subset. An *open covering* of $U$ is a family $(U_i)_{i\in I}$ of open subsets of $U$ (any index set) with $U=\bigcup_{i\in I}U_i$; it is regarded as the covering $\mathcal U=\{U_i\to U\}_{i\in I}$ of the Zariski site $X_{\rm Zar}$, the site of open subschemes of $X$ with inclusions as morphisms and jointly surjective open families as coverings [def-sc-zariski-site], in which the fibre product $U_{i_0}\times_U\cdots\times_UU_{i_p}$ is the intersection $U_{i_0\ldots i_p}=U_{i_0}\cap\cdots\cap U_{i_p}$ with its inclusions and the projection omitting the $j$-th factor is the inclusion $U_{i_0\ldots i_{p+1}}\subseteq U_{i_0\ldots\hat{i_j}\ldots i_{p+1}}$; $\check H^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)$ denotes the Cech cohomology [def-weil-pbc-site-cech-complex] of the underlying presheaf of abelian groups $W\mapsto\mathcal F(W)$ of $\mathcal F$ on $X_{\rm Zar}$ for $\mathcal U$ (degree $p$ term $\prod_{(i_0,\ldots,i_p)\in I^{p+1}}\mathcal F(U_{i_0\ldots i_p})$, alternating sum of restrictions as differential). Let $\Sigma$ be a set of open coverings of $U$ which is cofinal (for every open covering $(V_j)_{j\in J}$ of $U$ there is $(U_i)_{i\in I}\in\Sigma$ such that every $U_i$ is contained in some $V_j$) and such that $\check H^1(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)=0$ for every $\mathcal U\in\Sigma$. Then $\varphi_U:\mathcal G(U)\to\mathcal H(U)$ is surjective. (Stacks states this for any ringed space.)

proof.text: **Step 1 (sectionwise kernel).** Short exactness [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence] gives that $\iota$ is a monomorphism with image $\ker\varphi$, $\varphi\iota=0$, and $\varphi$ is an epimorphism. Thus $\iota$ identifies $\mathcal F$ with the kernel of $\varphi$. Kernels of sheaves of modules are computed sectionwise [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Consequently for each open $W$, $\iota_W$ is injective with image $\ker\varphi_W$.

source.place: Tag 01EU, label lemma-ses-cech-h1, proof, kernel identification of differences; Modules on Sites 03DA for sectionwise kernels

proof.text: **Step 2 (local lifts).** Fix $h\in\mathcal H(U)$. Set $P(W)=\mathcal H(W)/\varphi_W(\mathcal G(W))$ and let $q:\mathcal H\to P^\#$ be the map to its sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. Cokernels are sheafifications of sectionwise cokernels [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], so $P^\#=\operatorname{Coker}\varphi=0$ since $\varphi$ is an epimorphism. Therefore $h\in\ker q_U$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-cokernel-local-image] to the morphism $\varphi:\mathcal G\to\mathcal H$ on $(X,\mathcal O_X)$: its statement identifies $\ker q$ with sections locally in the image. Hence an open covering $U=\bigcup_jV_j$ and sections $g'_j\in\mathcal G(V_j)$ exist with $\varphi(g'_j)=h|_{V_j}$.

source.place: Tag 01EU, label lemma-ses-cech-h1, proof, choice of local lifts; local-image criterion from the cited module cokernel node

proof.text: **Step 3 (refinement).** By cofinality choose $\mathcal U=(U_i)_{i\in I}\in\Sigma$ refining $(V_j)$. Choose $j(i)$ with $U_i\subseteq V_{j(i)}$, and let $g_i=g'_{j(i)}|_{U_i}$. Restriction commutes with $\varphi$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], so $\varphi(g_i)=h|_{U_i}$. By hypothesis $\check H^1(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)=0$.

source.place: Tag 01EU, label lemma-ses-cech-h1, proof, choice of covering satisfying (a) and (b)

proof.text: **Step 4 (cocycle).** On $U_{ij}=U_i\cap U_j$ the section $\gamma_{ij}=g_j|-g_i|$ maps under $\varphi$ to $h|-h|=0$. Step 1 gives a unique $c_{ij}\in\mathcal F(U_{ij})$ with $\iota(c_{ij})=\gamma_{ij}$. These form a degree-one cochain [def-weil-pbc-site-cech-complex]. On $U_{ijk}$ its differential is $c_{jk}|-c_{ik}|+c_{ij}|$. Since $\iota$ commutes with restriction [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], its image equals $(g_k|-g_j|)-(g_k|-g_i|)+(g_j|-g_i|)=0$. Injectivity of $\iota_{U_{ijk}}$ gives $d^1c=0$. All restrictions in this identity are to the same triple intersection.

source.place: Tag 01EU, label lemma-ses-cech-h1, proof, sections s_{i_0i_1}; implicit cocycle identity written out

proof.text: **Step 5 (correction).** By [def-weil-pbc-site-cech-complex], $\check H^1=\ker d^1/\operatorname{im}d^0$. Vanishing of this quotient and Step 4 yield $t=(t_i)\in\prod_i\mathcal F(U_i)$ with $c=d^0t$, so $c_{ij}=t_j|-t_i|$. Put $\widetilde g_i=g_i-\iota(t_i)$. On $U_{ij}$ their difference is $\widetilde g_j|-\widetilde g_i|=\gamma_{ij}-\iota(c_{ij})=0$, using naturality of $\iota$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Also $\varphi(\widetilde g_i)=h|_{U_i}$ because $\varphi\iota=0$.

source.place: Tag 01EU, label lemma-ses-cech-h1, proof, sections t_i and corrected sections s_i-t_i

proof.text: **Step 6 (gluing).** The sheaf axiom for $\mathcal G$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] glues the compatible $\widetilde g_i$ uniquely to $g\in\mathcal G(U)$. Naturality gives $\varphi_U(g)|_{U_i}=h|_{U_i}$ for every $i$. The uniqueness part of the sheaf axiom for $\mathcal H$ implies $\varphi_U(g)=h$. Since $h$ was arbitrary, $\varphi_U$ is surjective. This also covers $U=\emptyset$: sheaves of modules have only the zero section there, and an empty compatible family glues uniquely.

source.place: Tag 01EU, label lemma-ses-cech-h1, proof, gluing of the corrected sections
